title: Phục hồi hay giam giữ · Problems / Solutions
prompt: Some societies are considering using community-based rehabilitation for more non-violent offenders. What problems could this create, and what measures could be taken to address them?
instructions: Give reasons for your answer and include any relevant examples from your own knowledge or experience. Write at least 250 words.

grammar.name: Đối chiếu hoặc đồng thời với while

grammar.why: Trong câu “Community rehabilitation changes the setting of punishment while retaining obligations intended to prevent further offending.”, while nối hai diễn biến hoặc yêu cầu cần xét cùng nhau; ở đây phải giữ cả hai phía để không biến điều kiện giới hạn thành phủ nhận toàn bộ lợi ích. Không nói không bạo lực nghĩa là không có nguy hiểm. Mức nguy cơ cá nhân, lịch sử vi phạm và nạn nhân cần xem riêng; tỷ lệ hoàn thành chương trình chưa đủ chứng minh an toàn.

paragraphs: Community rehabilitation changes the setting of punishment while retaining obligations intended to prevent further offending. Weakly supervised orders can expose victims to further harm, so expansion requires treatment capacity, individual risk assessment and enforceable responses to breaches.

Weak supervision can undermine public confidence and fail to protect victims. Without staff and treatment capacity, a community order may exist mainly on paper. Failure to monitor compliance or respond to breaches can leave victims exposed and undermine trust, while the offender receives neither the support nor the credible boundaries needed for rehabilitation. A community sentence preserves useful social ties only if supervision and treatment are available; an unenforced order cannot produce the same rehabilitative mechanism. A victim may still face intimidation from an offender whose original conviction was classified as non-violent, making offence labels an inadequate substitute for assessing current risk. If appointments are missed repeatedly without a response, both the offender and the victim may conclude that the conditions have little practical force.

Eligibility should reflect individual risk and programmes should have enforceable conditions. Programme capacity and enforceable conditions are essential, with individual risk assessment preventing a broad offence label from replacing attention to victims and future harm. Supervisors need manageable caseloads and a clear route for reporting breaches, because imposing more conditions cannot improve victim protection if nobody has the time or authority to check compliance. Individual assessments should therefore guide eligibility, and supervisors must be able to respond promptly to breaches, with treatment places genuinely available rather than repeatedly postponing the support on which rehabilitation depends.

Overall, eligibility should reflect individual risk, and evaluation should examine reoffending and victim protection alongside employment and compliance, rather than assume that non-violent classification guarantees safety.
